questions.title: Cross Join Definition
questions.description: What does a CROSS JOIN produce?
questions.Option1: Every row of the first table paired with every row of the second table
questions.Option2: Only rows that satisfy a matching condition
questions.Option3: The union of both tables' rows
questions.Option4: One row per matching pair, dropping duplicates

questions.title: Cross Join Row Count Math
questions.description: A CROSS JOIN of an 8-row players table and a 5-row rounds table returns how many rows?

questions.title: Why Self Joins Need Aliases
questions.description: Why must a self join give the two copies of a table different aliases?
questions.Option2: Because aliases are required by COUNT
questions.Option3: So each copy can be referenced by a distinct name
questions.Option4: To hide the table name from users

questions.title: Halving Pairs With Less Than
questions.description: With 8 players, what does COUNT(*) return for a self join using ON a.id < b.id?

questions.title: Natural Join Match Rule
questions.description: NATURAL JOIN matches rows using which columns?
questions.Option1: Every column name the two tables share
questions.Option3: The first column of each table

questions.title: Ambiguous Column Error
questions.description: SELECT name FROM players a, players b; fails in SQLite. Why?
questions.Option1: Self joins are forbidden in SQLite
questions.Option3: Aliases must be declared with AS
questions.Option4: name is ambiguous — both copies of players provide it

questions.title: Cross Join Count Snippet
questions.description: Players (8 rows) and club_halls (4 rows) are seeded. What does this query return?
questions.codesnippet: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players CROSS JOIN club_halls;

questions.title: Deterministic Pair Order
questions.description: For a self-join pair listing (a.id < b.id), which ORDER BY makes the output fully deterministic?

questions.title: Same Club Pair Count Snippet
questions.description: Four clubs hold two players each. What does this query return?
questions.codesnippet: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players a JOIN players b ON a.id < b.id AND a.club = b.club;

questions.title: Three Table Join ON Count
questions.description: Joining games to players (white) and players (black) requires how many ON clauses?

questions.title: Filtered Cross Equals Conditional Join
questions.description: CROSS JOIN players a, players b WHERE a.club <> b.club versus JOIN players b ON a.club <> b.club — what is true?
questions.Option2: JOIN ON is always faster and drops duplicates
questions.Option4: They return the same rows — the filtered cross join matches the conditional join

questions.title: Natural Join Without Shared Columns
questions.description: Two tables share NO column names. What does NATURAL JOIN between them do?
questions.Option1: It falls back to a cartesian product, like CROSS JOIN

questions.title: Duplicate Alias Crash Snippet
questions.description: What is wrong with this query?
questions.Option1: It runs but shows black players as white
questions.Option2: It runs but doubles the rows
questions.Option3: The alias w is used twice — duplicate table alias error
questions.Option4: games must come last in the FROM clause
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT w.name
FROM games g
JOIN players w ON w.id = g.white_id
JOIN players w ON w.id = g.black_id;

questions.title: Rating Tie Pair Count
questions.description: Exactly two players share a rating and all other ratings are unique. How many rows does ON a.id < b.id AND a.rating = b.rating return?

questions.title: Ordered Versus Unordered Pairs
questions.description: How do a.id <> b.id and a.id < b.id differ in a self join?
questions.Option1: a.id < b.id lists each unordered pair once; a.id <> b.id lists both directions

questions.title: Join Chain Column Source Snippet
questions.description: In this query, which clause matches the black player?
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT g.round_no, w.name, b.name
FROM games g
JOIN players w ON w.id = g.white_id
JOIN players b ON b.id = g.black_id;

questions.title: Natural Self Join Surprise
questions.description: What does this query return for any 8-row table?
questions.codesnippet: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players NATURAL JOIN players;

questions.title: Triple Cross Product Size
questions.description: players has 8 rows, openings 5, rounds 5. What does this return?
questions.codesnippet:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM players CROSS JOIN openings CROSS JOIN rounds;

questions.title: Half Matrix Versus Full Matrix
questions.description: For 8 players, COUNT(*) with self join ON a.id <> b.id returns 56. What does ON a.id < b.id return, and why?
questions.Option4: 0 — an id cannot differ from itself

questions.title: Mixing CROSS JOIN and JOIN ON
questions.description: FROM players a CROSS JOIN players b JOIN club_halls h ON h.club = a.club WHERE a.club <> b.club — is this valid SQLite?
questions.Option1: Invalid — CROSS JOIN cannot be mixed with other joins
questions.Option2: Invalid — WHERE must come before the joins
questions.Option3: Valid — the ON clause binds only to the club_halls join
questions.Option4: Valid — the ON applies to the entire join tree
